title: Contract Enforcer + Launch-time Drift Detector for Config/Model Rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a lightweight policy engine (Contract Enforcer) and a launch-time drift detector (DriftWatcher) that together enforce per-metric contracts during Canary and A/B rollouts. The goal is to stop or automatically shrink traffic for model/config changes when key quality or latency signals deviate beyond configured tolerances before a full rollout completes.
acceptance_criteria: Contract Enforcer can be configured per-rollout with at least: primary metric, tolerance window, minimum sample size, comparison baseline (previous model or production golden set)
DriftWatcher computes online drift and delta metrics (BLEU/ROUGE-like proxy, token-distribution KL, latency P95) within the canary cohort and emits structured events to the rollout controller
When a contract violation is detected and exceeds automatic-action thresholds the rollout controller reduces canary traffic to 0 or triggers the configured rollback policy without manual intervention
Telemetry surfaced in Console: contract verdicts, per-cohort metric trends, reason for rollback, and links to detailed eval artifacts
End-to-end automated test exercises synthetic regression on a canary and confirms automatic rollback is executed and logged
implementation_notes: Architectural approach: keep Contract Enforcer as a config-driven middleware that subscribes to per-route eval streams and exposes a gRPC API for the rollout controller to query verdicts
DriftWatcher will compute lightweight batch statistics on sampled responses (n <= 1k / minute in high-throughput routes) to avoid adding significant CPU overhead
Use existing eval harness to run golden-set comparisons; add an online mode that accepts sampled requests and returns metric deltas
Fallback: if eval pipeline is degraded, controller will fall back to configured safe-mode (pause rollout and alert) rather than blind continuation
Store per-rollout policy and recent verdicts in the rollout-store (extend current schema with contract_verdicts[] as strings)
Security: Contract Enforcer will only have read access to minimal artifact buckets; no customer data will be persisted beyond short-lived evaluation buffers
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Spike (dev env): implement Contract Enforcer prototype and unit tests (2 sprints)
Phase 1 - Internal beta (staging): wire DriftWatcher into a staging Canary for one non-critical model route; run shadow rollouts for 2 weeks
Phase 2 - Controlled customer pilot: enable automatic shrink-to-zero for rollouts marked as "automatic" for low-risk customers
Phase 3 - General availability: enable on by default for internal traffic; provide opt-out flag and UI in Console to tune tolerances
monitoring_metrics: contract_verdict_rate: fraction of samples judged as passing per-minute
contract_violation_count: number of unique violations per rollout
automatic_action_count: number of times controller performed automatic shrink/rollback
time_to_detect: time from rollout start to first violation detection
false_positive_rate: measured via synthetic golden regressions in staging
test_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluation logic (boundary tolerances, sample size gating)
Integration test: simulated canary with injected synthetic regressions that exceed thresholds -> expect automatic shrink-to-zero
Load test: ensure DriftWatcher adds <5% CPU and <3ms median added latency at 8k rps across sampled routes
E2E canary test: run in staging against a historical model diff to validate metric computations match offline evals
